$description: PROPOSED `when` additions for the UNANIMOUS rows Dave ratified. s253-D1 shape (GATE — PROSE, one string). NEVER APPLIED by this script.

knowledge/components/input-fields.meta.j.when: entry = free text AND expected answer fits ONE line AND no fixed option list exists AND the value is not money, a date, a time or a secret — the default text-entry field; beats textarea (proposed "the answer may span multiple lines") whenever the answer is a name, a reference or a phone number; yields to amount-input when the value is money, to date-picker / time-picker when it is a date or time, to secure-entry when it is a one-time code or PIN, and to dropdown or combobox whenever the answer must come from a list at all (Carbon: free text there "is likely to result in an error").

knowledge/components/textarea.meta.json.when: entry = free text AND the answer may run to more than one line AND there is no fixed option list AND a length limit is shown only where a real limit exists — beats input-fields (proposed "the answer fits one line") the moment a sentence is expected rather than a value — notes to approvers, a reason for payment, a secure message body; yields to input-fields for anything shorter (GOV.UK, verbatim: "enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number"); the counter is added only when a limit genuinely exists (GOV.UK: "Only use the character count component when there is a good reason for limiting").

knowledge/components/icon-button.meta.js.when: the control performs an action AND space is tight OR the glyph is universal AND an accessible name is supplied AND the hit target is at least 44x44 AND a tooltip carries the label — CANON on the first half (roles.json: "space is tight and the glyph is universal"); beats button only where the glyph is unambiguous — our own meta: "Use a labelled Button when the action is not unambiguous from a glyph alone"; the tooltip is not optional company: Atlassian ("Use tooltips with icon buttons to display the button label") and Polaris ("Be provided for icon-only buttons") both make it a requirement, which our meta states only as an antiPattern.

knowledge/components/alert.meta.json.when: the message is IN FLOW (inside the page or form it refers to) AND it persists until resolved or dismissed AND it carries a status glyph and a title, never colour alone AND an error alert never auto-dismisses — CANON-ADJACENT — our own purpose already states the three-way rule: "Use Toast for transient confirmations and Banner for page-level persistent messages; use inline field validation (Input-fields) for single-control errors"; beats toast (proposed "transient, no answer required") whenever the reader must act; beats banner (proposed "the condition governs the whole page or session") whenever the message belongs to one form or section — Atlassian draws the identical line: "For messages with information affecting the whole site, use a banner"; yields to inline field validation for a single control.

knowledge/components/popover.meta.json.when: the content is STRUCTURED and FOCUSABLE AND it opens on CLICK from a labelled trigger AND it does not scroll AND it is non-modal (no focus trap, no aria-modal) AND only one is open — CANON-ADJACENT — our purpose already carries the three-way rule: "If the user can act inside it, it is a Popover; if it is a sentence of help text, it is a Tooltip; if it must interrupt, it is a Modal"; Atlassian states both halves independently ("For interactive overlays, use the modal dialog component" / "For non-essential, non-interactive messages, use the tooltip component"); yields to drawer or modals once the content scrolls (our antiPatterns[2], Atlassian: "Don't make popups that scroll", Carbon: past four columns wide use a modal).

knowledge/components/timeline.meta.json.when: records >= 2 AND time IS the structure AND every record has ALREADY HAPPENED AND entries are not buttons AND order is newest-first with date headings — roles.json when: "time is the structure, records have happened"; beats list-items when the date rail is the reading rather than a sort order; yields to list-items inside a date group the moment entries must open (our AP1), and never borrows Progress-tracker's aria-current because there is no current step (our AP0).

knowledge/components/view-options.meta.j.when: NEVER — superseded 2026-07-24; the view switch is Segmented-control — carries no selection criterion because it is not a choice any composer should make: filter-toolbar-bar's AP1 already says "Consuming View-options instead of Segmented-control for the view switch — View-options was superseded"; the honest `when` here is a redirect, not a predicate.

knowledge/components/Chart-boxplot.meta..when: answers = distribution AND categories >= 2 AND each category carries a five-number summary AND span.cols <= 8 — roles.json when: "distribution per category"; beats Chart-histogram (roles.json: "distribution, one variable") whenever the spread must be read PER CATEGORY; yields to it when variables = 1 and the bin shape is the claim.
knowledge/components/Chart-boxplot.meta.._existing_when: answers=distribution AND categories ≥ 2 AND each category carries a five-number summary (median · IQR · whiskers · outliers) — beats Chart-histogram (76, "distribution, one variable") whenever the spread must be read PER CATEGORY; yields to it when variables=1 and the bin shape is the claim. span.cols max 8 because the FIT hooks are not wired (this meta's own responsive rule).

knowledge/components/Chart-candlestick.m.when: answers = change-over-time AND shape = periods × OHLC (open · high · low · close per session) — roles.json when: "OHLC per period"; beats chart-line (roles.json: "change-over-time") only when all four price points per period are the claim; yields to chart-line whenever one measure's path is enough.
knowledge/components/Chart-candlestick.m._existing_when: answers=change-over-time AND shape=periods × OHLC (open · high · low · close per session) — beats chart-line (88, "change-over-time") only when all four price points per period are the claim; yields to chart-line whenever one measure's path is enough.

knowledge/components/Chart-histogram.met.when: answers = distribution AND variables = 1 AND bins = contiguous (no inter-bar gap) AND baseline = 0 — roles.json when: "distribution, one variable"; beats Chart-boxplot (roles.json: "distribution per category") when the frequency shape of ONE variable is the claim; yields to Chart-boxplot when categories >= 2; the no-gap rule is not cosmetic — the FT gives the same reason: "keep the gaps between columns small to highlight the 'shape' of the data".
knowledge/components/Chart-histogram.met._existing_when: answers=distribution AND variables=1 AND bins=contiguous (no inter-bar gap) — beats Chart-boxplot (60, "distribution per category") when the frequency shape of ONE variable is the claim rather than the spread per category; yields to Chart-boxplot when categories ≥ 2.

knowledge/components/limits-meter.meta.j.when: INHERITS meter's gate, variant = allowance: the value is a cap being spent against AND full = BLOCKED, not done — a thin category alias of meter.meta.json (s210-D5); carries no independent when because writing spec into the alias is an explicit antiPattern on the parent — the reading is "how much of my limit is left", which is what roles.json already names.

knowledge/components/app-shell-focused.m.when: primaryNavigation = absent AND breadcrumbs = absent AND search = absent AND exits = 1 AND job.count = 1 — the only frame defined by removal; beats every other shell (roles.json: all six carry navigation) whenever abandoning the task is the failure mode — authentication, a wizard, a passcode; yields to app-shell-top-nav the moment the user must be able to go somewhere else.

knowledge/components/template-wizard.met.when: steps >= 2 AND order is enforced AND next is gated AND a review step precedes the end AND the end is a receipt — beats template-create-edit (proposed "one page, no enforced order") on order; composes app-shell-focused (roles.json when: "one job, no navigation (auth, wizard)") and borrows the step mechanism whole from Stepper.

knowledge/components/template-confirmati.when: position = end of an instruction AND order = message, then FACTS, then actions, then what-happens-next AND a reference is shown if one exists — beats the Confirmation component (roles.json feedback role) because a confirmation PAGE is also the RECEIPT — that reordering is the template's whole contribution; ends a flow that template-wizard began.

knowledge/components/template-error.meta.when: cause in (404, 500) AND RAG colour = unbound AND no support semantics invented AND one page serves ALL unexpected failures — beats template-empty (proposed "the query succeeded and returned nothing") because here the page could not be produced at all; beats an inline Alert (slice A) because the failure is the PAGE, not a field.
